key_insight: Rotational equivariance and nonlocality together improve learned subgrid-scale closures, with the biggest gains appearing in the equivariant nonlocal model.
engineering_relevance: For LES turbulence modeling, building in symmetry can reduce parameter needs and improve generalization across flow conditions, making closures more practical for real engineering applications.
method: Compare data-augmented non-equivariant vs equivariant tensorial architectures
Test both pointwise and nonlocal model variants at matched parameter counts
Evaluate spatiotemporal, anisotropy, and Reynolds-number generalization in turbulent channel flow
evidence_signal: The equivariant nonlocal model achieved the highest correlation on every generalization test at about half the parameter count of its non-equivariant counterpart, and was also more data-efficient.
watch_item: Pointwise models did not beat the analytical Clark baseline, so equivariance alone may not be enough without sufficient receptive field or nonlocal context.
paper_title: Rotational equivariance and locality in data-driven subgrid-scale closures
